author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Diocese of Lansing announces novena for ordinands ahead of June ordination
text:
The Diocese of Lansing announced on May 27 that a Novena will be held from May 28 to June 5, inviting the faithful to pray for six men preparing for ordination as priests and deacons. The ordination ceremony is scheduled for Saturday, June 6, at Saint Thomas Aquinas parish in East Lansing.
The ordinands are Rev. Mr. Joshua Mark Bauer from St. Elizabeth in Tecumseh; Rev. Mr. Jacob John Derry from St. John the Evangelist in Fenton; Rev. Mr. Ryan Scott Ferrigan from St. Martha in Okemos; Rev. Mr. Peter Casey Randolph from Christ the King in Ann Arbor; James Burleson Bonar also from Christ the King in Ann Arbor; and Paul Edward Keenan from St. John the Baptist in Ypsilanti.
Participants are encouraged to pray an Our Father, Hail Mary, and Glory Be each day during the Novena period with specific intentions assigned to each day, including thanksgiving for baptism, discernment of vocation, generosity in accepting one’s calling, support for single life dedicated to God, protection of vocations, holy marriages and families as sources of vocations, and abundance of ordained clergy and religious brothers and sisters serving the Church.
A prayer provided by the diocese reads: “Hear us, we beseech you, Lord our God,
and pour out on these your servants the blessing of the Holy Spirit,
that these men who are to be consecrated to your service,
may be surrounded by your rich and unfailing grace.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen!”
The Diocese encourages all members to join this spiritual effort leading up to ordination day as a sign of support for those entering ministry roles within their communities.
The Diocese of Lansing was established in 1937 and was first headed by Most Reverend Joseph H. Albers; it now encompasses several counties including Clinton, Eaton, Genesee, Hillsdale, Ingham, Jackson, Lenawee, Livingston, Shiawassee and Washtenaw while serving more than 185,000 Catholics under Bishop Earl Boyea since 2008, according to the Diocese of Lansing .
